meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided, Hale, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, on what basis did you give him a zero?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
"The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." I'll check that myself tonight, Hale, but a seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a mistake, not proof of anything. What else do you have?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and I'm writing down exactly what you just said for the principal. The zero comes off, or I'm going upstairs when we're done here.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this essay goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and is ready to take it to the principal.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" earned a flat okay, because you owned the process in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" cost the most, because it dragged in Claire's appeal, which she won and has never forgiven the school for.
Try next time: after the misquoted line, when she asked what else you had, answer with a dated page of Owen's essay she can check herself instead of bringing up Claire.
